printed page 74259)
financial and operating metrics. The Exchange further believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, as binary KPI options would be subject to the Exchange's existing rules governing the listing and trading of options. The Exchange believes expanding the universe of binary options will benefit investors, particularly retail investors and other investors who prefer simplicity, as a complementary offering to current exchange-traded options.
The proposed rule change will permit the Exchange to list binary KPI options on a national securities exchange as alternatives to products that are structured in substantially the same manner as binary options currently available in the OTC market and on other platforms. The Exchange understands investors have traded binary options similar to the proposed binary options in OTC markets for many years but may prefer to trade such options in a listed environment to receive the benefits of trading listed options. These benefits include: (1) enhanced efficiency in initiating and closing out positions; (2) increased market transparency; and (3) heightened contra-party creditworthiness. The Exchange believes the proposed rule change may encourage liquidity to shift from the OTC market onto the Exchange, which the Exchange believes would increase market transparency as well as enhance the process of price discovery conducted on the Exchange through increased order flow. The proposed rule change is intended to provide a market for binary KPI options as a standardized product without the credit risk of an individual issuer. By providing a listed and standardized market for more classes of binary options, the Exchange seeks to attract investors who desire the simplicity of a binary option with the certainty and safeguards of a regulated and standardized marketplace. Additionally, unlike an OTC binary option, counter-party credit risk for Exchange-listed binary KPI options is significantly reduced through the issuance and guarantee of the contracts by a registered clearing agency. Further, as an exchange-traded option, binary options will have the advantage of liquidity provided by Market Makers, which the Exchange believes may lead to tighter spreads than those in the OTC market. The Exchange also believes that standardization will enable more interested parties to become market participants.
In addition to the OTC market, various market platforms that are not registered as national securities exchanges currently offer products structured in substantively the same manner as binary options that the Exchange may list pursuant to current Rules and as proposed. These platforms offer binary option products overlying issuer KPI, which may be settled at varying points of the day (not just at the open and close of the trading day). However, as these venues are not national securities exchanges, they do not offer investors the benefits of centralized liquidity, market transparency, or securities regulations intended to protect investors. The Exchange believes listing competitive products on a national securities exchange would create a centralized and standardized marketplace for these products, which promotes price discovery and transparency, within an established regulatory framework designed to afford investors in securities with important protections. In other words, the Exchange believes its proposal offers a more transparent platform than the OTC market or other market platforms offer. It would contribute to leveling the playing field with these alternative markets and provide investors with safeguards associated with Commission and SRO oversight of the trading activity in these exchange-listed binary KPI options.
Ultimately, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change will provide investors with greater trading tools and opportunities and flexibility, resulting in investors having additional means to carry out their investment objectives and manage their risk exposures through products listed and traded on a national securities exchange. The Exchange believes the proposed rule change will offer market participants a simplified, transparent, and limited risk investment choice that may be more aligned with their specific timing needs, investment and hedging strategies, and risk tolerances. The Exchange believes it benefits the investing public to continue to enhance its listed product offerings to respond to continuously changing needs of investors and to a continuously changing competitive environment.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, because binary KPI options will be available to all market participants who wish to trade such options on the same terms and in the same manner (including with respect to the payout terms and amount). All market participants will be subject to the same rules applicable to binary KPI options, as described in this proposed rule change. Except as set forth in the proposed rule change, binary KPI options will trade in the same manner as binary KPI options on Cboe.
The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act, because binary KPI options have been approved to be listed on Cboe and other options exchanges may propose similar products. Additionally, as noted above, substantively similar products to binary KPI options, as proposed, are available in the OTC market and various other markets.
The Exchange notes that it operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues who offer similar products. The Exchange believes the proposed rule change will provide investors with a comparable alternative to the OTC market and other venues. The Exchange believes it may be a more attractive alternative to Cboe, the OTC market and these other venues, as market participants will benefit from being able to trade these options in an exchange environment, which provides, among other things: (1) enhanced efficiency in initiating and closing out positions; (2) increased market transparency; and (3) heightened contra-party creditworthiness. As a result, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change may relieve any burden on, or otherwise promote, competition, as it will allow the Exchange to offer a securities exchange-listed alternative to the products currently available in these other markets.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section
(
printed page 74260)
19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
42
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
43
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder.
[
44
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
45
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
http://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include File Number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-97 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to File Number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-97. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
http://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to File Number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-97 and should be submitted on or before December 9, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
46
]
J. Matthew DeLesDernier,
Deputy Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106897; File No. SR-CBOE-2026-085]
November 13, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on November 2, 2026, Cboe Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “Cboe Options”) proposes to amend its Fees Schedule to (1) apply the existing SPX/SPXW Electronic Execution Surcharge to S&P 500 Index (“SPX”) options with a.m.-settlement trading under the OSI root symbol SPXO (“SPXO”), and add SPXO to each other provision of the Fees Schedule that currently references SPXW;
[
3
]
(2) amend the fees, initiating credits, and credit cap applicable to Qualified Contingent Cross (“QCC”) orders; (3) amend the Market-Maker manual (open outcry) transaction fee for Multiply Listed options classes to distinguish between Penny and non-Penny classes; (4) adopt a new Floor Broker Break-Up Credits Program for Floor Broker orders executed against Market-Makers on the trading floor, and make related amendments to the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Rebate Program and Floor Broker Sliding Scale Supplemental Rebate Program; (5) amend footnote 55 to define Index Binaries as binary options on XSP, MRUT, DJX and MGTN, and replace references to “XSPBX” elsewhere in the Fees Schedule with references to “Index Binaries (55)”; (6) adopt a fee holiday for Market-Maker orders in Index Binaries executed electronically and adding liquidity; (7) amend the transaction fee for Index Binaries where the premium is greater than or equal to $1.00 to a flat $0.01 per contract for fee codes HC (Customer), HD (Clearing Trader Permit Holder Proprietary, Broker-Dealer, Joint Back-Office, Non-Trading Permit Holder Market Maker, and Professional) and HB (Market-Maker, Electronic, Removing-Liquidity); and (8) adopt a Flex AIM Response Fee and a corresponding FLEX break-up credit for Customer Agency orders. The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​options/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​cone/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of
(
printed page 74261)
the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend its Fees Schedule, effective November 1, 2026.
SPXO Electronic Execution Surcharge and Other Conforming Changes
First, the Exchange proposes to amend its Fees Schedule to apply the SPX/SPXW Electronic Execution Surcharge to SPXO options. The Exchange intends to list SPX options that are a.m.-settled under the OSI root symbol SPXO beginning on November 9, 2026.
[
4
]
Currently, the Fees Schedule assesses an Electronic Execution Surcharge of $0.14 per contract on electronic executions in SPXW options
[
5
]
(noting that this is different than the Electronic Execution Surcharge of $0.21 for SPX).
[
6
]
The Exchange proposes to amend the Fees Schedule to provide that the $0.14 per contract surcharge will also apply to electronic executions in SPXO options. In addition, the Exchange proposes to add SPXO to each other provision of the Fees Schedule that currently references SPXW (
e.g.,
by amending references to “SPX (incl SPXW)” to read “SPX (incl SPXW and SPXO),” and references to “SPX/SPXW” to read “SPX/SPXW/SPXO”), including in the Underlying Symbol List A rate table, the Index License Surcharge, the Floor Broker Solicitation Surcharge, the SPX/SPXW/SPXO Liquidity Provider Sliding Scale, the SCORe Program, the Market-Maker Tier Appointment Fees, the Floor Broker Trading Surcharge, the Floor Brokerage Fees and Floor Brokerage Fees Discount Scale, the GTH1 and GTH2 SPX/SPXW/SPXO LMM Incentive Programs, and footnote 41, so that SPXO is treated in the same manner as SPXW throughout the Fees Schedule. The Exchange intends to launch SPXO options on November 9, 2026. Accordingly, no SPXO fees will be assessed prior to the launch date.
The Exchange believes that SPXO options are comparable to SPXW options, as both are weekly options on the S&P 500 Index exclusively listed on the Exchange (the primary difference is that SPXO options are a.m.-settled while SPXW options are p.m.-settled), and that it is therefore appropriate to assess the same Electronic Execution Surcharge on electronic executions in both products.
QCC Fees, Initiating Credits, and Credit Cap
Next, the Exchange proposes to amend the fees, credits, and credit cap applicable to QCC orders.
[
7
]
Currently, the Exchange assesses a fee of $0.18 per contract on Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer QCC orders (fee code QN), and a fee of $0.00 per contract on Customer and Professional Customer QCC orders. The Exchange proposes to increase the fee for Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer QCC orders from $0.18 to $0.20 per contract. Fees for Customer and Professional Customer QCC orders will remain unchanged.
The Exchange also currently provides a credit of $0.11 per contract to the initiating side of a QCC transaction, except that no credit is paid on Customer (C) to Customer (C) executions, Customer (C) to Professional (U) executions, Professional (U) to Professional (U) executions or Professional (U) to Customer (C).
[
8
]
The Exchange proposes to amend the initiating credit so that the amount of the credit depends on (i) the initiating side and (ii) the contra side. Specifically, as proposed, the initiator of a QCC transaction will receive (i) no credit where both the initiating and contra sides are Customer or Professional Customer orders (in accordance with current practice);
[
9
]
(ii) a credit for the initiating order of $0.18 per contract where only one side of the transaction is a Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer order; and (iii) a credit for the initiating order of $0.30 per contract where both sides of the transaction are Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer orders. To reflect this structure, the Exchange proposes to bifurcate the Per Contract Credit column of the QCC Rate Table into two sections, one for Customer and Professional (capacity codes C and U) and one for all other capacities, mirroring the existing fee structure, and to set forth the applicable credits for each. Because the exclusion of Customer-to-Customer, Customer-to-Professional, and Professional-to-Professional executions will be reflected in the proposed credit amounts themselves, the Exchange also proposes to delete the existing sentence in the QCC Rate Table Notes providing that credits will not be paid on such executions. The following table summarizes the current and proposed QCC fees and initiating credits:
Capacity
Current fee
Proposed fee
Current initiating credit
Proposed initiating credit
Customer, Professional Customer
$0.00
$0.00
$0.00 if contra Customer or Professional Customer; $0.11 otherwise
$0.00 if contra Customer or Professional Customer; $0.18 otherwise.
Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer
0.18
0.20
$0.11
$0.18 if contra Customer or Professional Customer; $0.30 otherwise.
Finally, the Exchange proposes to increase the maximum amount of QCC initiating credits a TPH may receive in a calendar month (the “QCC Credit Cap”) from $350,000 to $500,000. The Exchange notes that its current practice of aggregating affiliated TPHs with at least 75% common ownership for purposes of determining if the QCC
(
printed page 74262)
Credit Cap has been met will remain unchanged.
The proposed changes are designed to encourage TPHs to initiate additional QCC transactions on the Exchange. The increased QCC Credit Cap allows TPHs that initiate significant QCC volume to continue to earn credits on that volume and has been increased in connection with the changes to initiator credits.
Multiply Listed Market-Maker Manual Transaction Fees
Next, the Exchange proposes to amend the transaction fee assessed on Market-Maker orders executed manually (
i.e.,
in open outcry) in Multiply Listed options classes. Currently, the Exchange assesses a fee of $0.45 per contract on Market-Maker manual transactions in all Multiply Listed options classes, yielding fee code MB. The Exchange proposes to separate this fee by Penny and non-Penny classes. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to increase the fee for Market-Maker manual transactions in Penny classes (fee code MB) from $0.45 to $0.50 per contract and to adopt a fee of $0.95 per contract for Market-Maker manual transactions in non-Penny classes, which will yield new fee code ME.
The Exchange notes that it, like other options exchanges, commonly assesses different transaction fees for Penny and non-Penny classes,
[
10
]
reflecting the wider spreads and generally greater potential profitability of transactions in non-Penny classes.
The proposed fees are in line with those recently adopted by other options exchanges with physical trading floors. NYSE American recently amended its Fee Schedule to increase the fee for Market Maker Manual transactions in non-Penny issues from $0.50 to $0.90 per contract and then to $1.00 per contract effective November 1, 2026, while retaining a fee of $0.50 per contract for Market Maker Manual transactions in Penny issues.
[
11
]
Nasdaq PHLX likewise recently increased its Non-Penny Symbol Floor Options Transaction Charge for Lead Market Makers and Market Makers, and currently assesses its market makers a fee of $1.00 per contract for floor transactions in non-Penny symbols,
[
12
]
and BOX assesses its market makers a fee of $1.00 per contract for Qualified Open Outcry and FLEX Open Outcry Order orders for manual transactions in non-Penny classes.
[
13
]
Most recently, MIAX Sapphire increased the fee assessed to Floor Market Makers for QFO and cQFO transactions in non-Penny classes that trade against all other origins from $0.50 to $0.94 per contract, while retaining a fee of $0.50 per contract for such transactions in Penny classes.
[
14
]
The Exchange's proposed fee of $0.50 per contract in Penny classes is identical to the corresponding fees at NYSE American, and MIAX Sapphire, and its proposed fee of $0.95 per contract in non-Penny classes falls within the range of $0.94 to $1.00 per contract assessed by MIAX Sapphire and NYSE American (beginning November 1, 2026), Nasdaq PHLX, and BOX, and is lower than the fees assessed by NYSE American, Nasdaq PHLX, and BOX.
The Exchange believes that, taken together with the proposed Floor Broker Break-Up Credits Program described below, which is designed to attract additional Floor Broker order flow for execution against Market-Makers, the proposed fee changes will not discourage Market-Makers from continuing to participate in transactions on the trading floor.
Floor Broker Break-Up Credits Program
Next, the Exchange proposes to adopt a new Floor Broker Break-Up Credits Program (the “Floor Broker Program”) under the Floor Broker Programs section of the Fees Schedule. Currently, Floor Brokers may earn rebates under the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Rebate Program and the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Supplemental Rebate Program. As proposed, the Floor Broker Program will provide a rebate of $0.20 per contract in Penny classes and $0.25 per contract in non-Penny classes for an applicable trade executed by a Floor Broker against a Market-Maker on the trading floor. Consistent with the existing Floor Broker programs, the Floor Broker Program will apply to all products except Underlying Symbol List A (34), Sector Indexes (47), DJX, CBTX, MBTX, MGTN, MRUT, NANOS, SPEQX, SPESG, XSP, Index Binaries (55), and FLEX Micros. Rebates paid through the Floor Broker Program will be in lieu of rebates accrued under the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Rebate Program and the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Supplemental Rebate Program; however, volume executed under the Floor Broker Program will continue to count toward tier qualification under both of those programs. In connection with this change, the Exchange proposes to amend the notes to the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Rebate Program and the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Supplemental Rebate Program to delete the language providing that Non-Firm Facilitated rebates under those programs apply to the portion of Floor Broker orders executed against Market-Maker quotes or orders. As a result, Floor Broker orders executed against Market-Makers will receive the Floor Broker Program rebate rather than Non-Firm Facilitated rebates under the sliding scale programs, while such volume will continue to be counted for purposes of calculating Volume (and thus tier qualification) under the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Rebate Program, which already provides that Volume includes the portion of Floor Broker orders executed against Market-Maker quotes or orders. The Exchange also proposes to amend footnotes 24 and 33 to add the Floor Broker Break-Up Credits Program to the list of programs from which Index Binaries and FLEX Micro Options, respectively, are excluded, consistent with the treatment of the existing Floor Broker programs.
The proposed rebate is designed to incentivize Floor Brokers to bring additional order flow to the Exchange's trading floor for execution against Market-Makers, which the Exchange believes will increase liquidity and trading opportunities on the trading floor to the benefit of all market participants.
The proposed Floor Broker Program is in line with floor broker break-up credits recently adopted by other options exchanges. NYSE Arca and NYSE American each provide a rebate of $0.20 per contract for Manual trades executed by a Floor Broker against a Market Maker on the trading floor, in lieu of any rebates achieved through their manual billable rebate programs,
[
15
]
and Nasdaq PHLX recently adopted a $0.20 per contract rebate for open outcry floor executions that are contra a Lead Market Maker or Market Maker, in lieu of any Floor Broker Incentive Program rebate.
[
16
]
MIAX Sapphire likewise
(
printed page 74263)
provides a “Floor Broker Breakup Credit” to the Floor Broker that submits a QFO or cQFO for executions that trade with a Floor Market Maker, instead of the $0.10 Floor Broker rebate otherwise available, and recently increased that credit from $0.20 to $0.25 per contract in non-Penny classes, while retaining a credit of $0.20 per contract in Penny classes.
[
17
]
The Exchange's proposed Floor Broker Program rebates of $0.20 per contract in Penny classes and $0.25 per contract in non-Penny classes are in line with the the MIAX Sapphire Floor Broker Breakup Credit. Like MIAX Sapphire, the Exchange proposes a higher rebate in non-Penny classes in light of the higher proposed Market-Maker manual fee in non-Penny classes, which the Exchange believes appropriately balances the incentive provided to Floor Brokers with the fees assessed on the Market-Makers against which their orders trade and may encourage additional Floor Broker liquidity in non-Penny classes.
Index Binaries—Amendment to Footnote 55 and Replacement of References to XSPBX
Next, the Exchange proposes to (i) amend footnote 55 to provide that Index Binaries include binary options on XSP, MRUT, DJX and MGTN; and (ii) replace each other reference to “XSPBX” in the Fees Schedule with a reference to “Index Binaries (55),” so that each provision of the Fees Schedule that currently applies to, or excludes, XSPBX will apply to, or exclude, all Index Binaries. For purposes of the Fees Schedule, “Index Binaries” are binary index options, as defined in Rule 4.70, that are listed for trading on the Exchange and identified in footnote 55 of the Fees Schedule. The term “Binary Option” means an option contract having an exercise settlement amount that is established at the creation of an option and only two possible payoff outcomes: either a fixed amount equal to the exercise payout amount or nothing at all.
[
18
]
Effective October 1, 2026, the Exchange amended the Rate Table—Binary Options in its Fees Schedule to replace the fixed, premium-based transaction fees previously applicable to XSPBX options (
i.e.,
XSP binary options) with a tier-based constant transaction fee methodology applicable to “Index Binaries,” and adopted new footnote 55, which provides that “Index Binaries include XSPBX.”
[
19
]
In that filing, the Exchange noted that it anticipated adding other binary index options to footnote 55 in future amendments to the Fees Schedule as it lists binary index options on additional indexes. The Exchange is now (or shortly after this filing expects to be) listing binary index options on additional indexes and accordingly proposes to amend footnote 55 to provide that “Index Binaries include binary options on XSP, MRUT, DJX, and MGTN.” As a result, transaction fees for orders in DJX, MRUT, and MGTN binary options will be calculated in the same manner as such fees are calculated for XSP binary options today.
In addition to the Rate Table—Binary Options, XSPBX is currently referenced in a number of other provisions of the Fees Schedule that exclude XSPBX from certain volume calculations, incentive programs, caps, and surcharges. These include the Liquidity Provider Sliding Scale, the Volume Incentive Program (“VIP”), Break-Up Credits, the Marketing Fee, the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Rebate Program, the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Supplemental Rebate Program, the Order Router Subsidy (“ORS”) Program, and the Complex Order Router Subsidy (“CORS”) Program tables and notes, as well as footnotes 6, 10, 11, 22, 24, 29, 30, 35, 36, and 44 of the Fees Schedule. The Exchange proposes to replace each of these references to “XSPBX” with “Index Binaries (55),” rather than enumerating each individual Index Binary in each provision. As a result, each Index Binary, including DJX, MRUT and MGTN binary options, will be excluded from the same programs, volume calculations, caps, and surcharges from which XSP binary options are excluded today. This change does not alter the treatment of XSP binary options under the Fees Schedule and simplifies the Fees Schedule by ensuring that any product identified in footnote 55 is treated consistently throughout the Fees Schedule.
Index Binaries—Market-Maker Fee Holiday and Fees for Premiums of $1.00 or Greater
The Exchange also proposes to amend certain transaction fees applicable to Index Binaries. Currently, Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM orders in Index Binaries executed electronically and adding liquidity are assessed a flat fee of $0.05 per contract (fee code HA). The Exchange proposes to adopt a fee holiday for fee code HA to which such orders will be assessed a fee of $0.00 per contract. The proposed fee holiday is designed to encourage Market-Makers to participate and quote competitively in Index Binaries, including newly listed Index Binaries. Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM orders in Index Binaries executed manually will continue to be assessed a flat fee of $0.15 per contract (fee code HM).
Further, the Exchange proposes to amend the transaction fee applicable to Index Binaries yielding fee codes HB, HC, and HD where the premium is greater than or equal to $1.00. Currently, the fees for such transactions are $0.01184 per contract for Customer orders (fee code HC) and $0.01386 per contract for Non-Customer orders (fee codes HB and HD), which reflect an approximation derived from the tier-based constant (k) pricing methodology. The Exchange proposes to instead assess a flat fee of $0.01 per contract for all capacities where the premium is greater than or equal to $1.00. Fees for Index Binaries where the premium is less than $1.00 will continue to be calculated using the existing tier-based constant methodology. To reflect this change, the Exchange proposes to restructure the Rate Table—Binary Options to set forth, in separate columns, (i) the flat Transaction Fee Per Contract when the premium is greater than or equal to $1.00 ($0.01 for fee codes HC, HD, and HB) and (ii) the Tier Based Constant (k) when the premium is less than $1.00 (unchanged at 1.2% for fee code HC and 1.4% for fee codes HD and HB), and to retitle the fee calculation column as the “Fee Calculation when Premium is <$1.00.”
Flex AIM Response Fee and FLEX Break-Up Credit
Finally, the Exchange proposes to adopt a Flex AIM Response Fee and a corresponding FLEX break-up credit. Specifically, the Exchange proposes to add a new “Flex AIM Response Fee (20)” line item to each of the Rate Table—All Products Excluding Underlying Symbol List A (34) and Binary Options and the Rate Table—Underlying Symbol List A (34), pursuant to which the Exchange will assess a fee of $1.00 per contract on orders executed in FLEX AIM and FLEX SAM auctions that were initially entered as an AIM Response. The fee will apply to all capacities (C, F, L, M, B, N, U, and J) and to both Multiply Listed and proprietary products. The Exchange also proposes to amend footnote 20, which currently provides that applicable standard transaction fees will apply to all orders executed in
(
printed page 74264)
AIM, SAM, FLEX AIM, and FLEX SAM auctions that were initially entered an AIM Responses, to (i) limit that provision to AIM and SAM auctions and (ii) provide that orders in FLEX AIM and FLEX SAM auctions (excluding FLEX Micros) that were initially entered an AIM Responses will be charged the new, proposed fee. In addition, the Exchange proposes to revise the Break-Up Credits table to add a new line item providing a credit of $0.50 per contract to Customer (capacity code C) Agency orders executed in FLEX AIM and FLEX SAM in all underlying symbols excluding FLEX Micros, when the Agency Order trades against an AIM Response, and to make a conforming change to the notes for the existing Break-Up Credits to provide that those credits apply to orders executed in AIM and SAM (deleting the references to FLEX AIM and FLEX SAM). Given the custom nature of FLEX options and the lack of on-screen liquidity, the Exchange understands the efforts brokers take to price these options and source liquidity to trade against their customers' orders can be substantial. Therefore, the Exchange believes that the proposed fee and credit will help protect the price discovery efforts of the parties that initiate FLEX AIM and FLEX SAM auctions and compensate Customer Agency orders whose volume is broken up, thereby encouraging market participants to continue to bring FLEX order flow to the Exchange rather than to other exchanges or over-the-counter markets.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”) and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
20
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
21
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
22
]
requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange also believes the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(4) of the Act,
[
23
]
which requires that Exchange rules provide for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its TPHs and other persons using its facilities.
The Exchange operates in a highly competitive market. The Commission has repeatedly expressed its preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. There are currently 20 registered options exchanges competing for order flow, and no single options exchange has more than approximately 20% of the market share of executed volume.
[
24
]
Accordingly, the Exchange is subject to significant competitive forces in setting the terms on which it offers its services, particularly with respect to Multiply Listed options.
The Exchange believes that applying the SPX/SPXW Electronic Execution Surcharge to SPXO options is reasonable because SPXO options, like SPXW options, are weekly options on the S&P 500 Index, and the Exchange believes it is appropriate to apply the same surcharge to electronic executions in comparable products. The amount of the surcharge is not changing, and the proposed change merely extends an existing surcharge to a new product. The proposed change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the surcharge will apply equally to all electronic executions in SPXO options by all market participants subject to the surcharge (once the options are launched), in the same manner as it currently applies to SPXW options.
The Exchange believes that the proposed increase to the Non-Customer, Non-Professional Customer QCC fee from $0.18 to $0.20 per contract is reasonable because the proposed fee remains modest and, combined with the proposed increased initiating credits, is designed to maintain an attractive overall pricing structure for QCC transactions. The Exchange believes that the proposed tiered QCC initiating credit structure is reasonable because it is designed to incentivize TPHs to initiate QCC transactions on the Exchange by offering increased credits of $0.18 per contract and $0.30 per contract (as applicable), compared to the current $0.11 per contract credit. The Exchange believes it is reasonable to provide a greater credit for transactions when the initiator is Non-Professional/Non-Customer as their fees are higher (
i.e.,
a fee of $0.20 per contract for a Non-Professional/Non Customer compared to $0.00 per contract for Customer/Professional). Similarly, the Exchange believes that increasing the QCC Credit Cap from $350,000 to $500,000 is reasonable because it allows TPHs to earn credits on a greater amount of QCC volume, further incentivizing QCC order flow and is done in parallel with an increase to the per contract credit. The proposed changes are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because they will apply uniformly to all similarly situated participants.
The Exchange believes that the proposed Market-Maker manual transaction fees for Multiply Listed options classes of $0.50 per contract in Penny classes and $0.95 per contract in non-Penny classes are reasonable because they are in line with fees assessed by other options exchanges for similar transactions. In particular, NYSE Arca, NYSE American, and MIAX Sapphire each assess a fee of $0.50 per contract for market maker manual or floor transactions in Penny classes, and MIAX Sapphire assesses $0.94 per contract and NYSE American (beginning November 1, 2026), Nasdaq PHLX, and BOX each assess $1.00 per contract for such transactions in non-Penny classes, such that the Exchange's proposed non-Penny fee is within the range of, and in several instances lower than, the fees assessed by other exchanges with trading floors. The Exchange believes it is reasonable to assess a higher fee in non-Penny classes because non-Penny classes generally have wider spreads and therefore present greater potential profitability for Market-Makers, and because the Exchange, like other exchanges, already differentiates between Penny and non-Penny classes for other transaction fees. The Exchange further believes that the proposed fees, considered together with the proposed Floor Broker Program, will not discourage Market-Makers from participating in open outcry transactions, as the Floor Broker Program is designed to attract additional Floor Broker order flow with which Market-Makers may trade. The proposed fees are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because they will apply equally to all Market-Makers executing manual transactions in Multiply Listed
(
printed page 74265)
options classes. The Exchange believes it is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory to assess Market-Makers a higher manual fee than certain other market participants because Market-Makers benefit from the ability to interact with Floor Broker order flow made available in open outcry, and the differential is consistent with the fee structures of other options exchanges.
The Exchange believes that the proposed Floor Broker Program is reasonable because it is designed to incentivize Floor Brokers to bring additional order flow to the trading floor for execution against Market-Makers, thereby increasing liquidity and execution opportunities on the trading floor. The proposed rebate is also in line with comparable floor broker break-up credits recently adopted by NYSE Arca, NYSE American, Nasdaq PHLX, and MIAX Sapphire, each of which provides a rebate of $0.20 per contract for floor broker executions against market makers on the trading floor, and is in line with the MIAX Sapphire Floor Broker Breakup Credit of $0.20 per contract in Penny classes and $0.25 per contract in non-Penny classes. The Exchange believes it is reasonable to provide a higher rebate in non-Penny classes as fees are higher for non-penny classes.
[
25
]
The Exchange also believes it is reasonable to pay the rebate in lieu of rebates under the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Rebate Program and the Floor Broker Sliding Scale Supplemental Rebate Program, and to make conforming amendments to those programs so that Non-Firm Facilitated rebates no longer apply to the portion of Floor Broker orders executed against Market-Makers, as doing so avoids paying duplicative rebates on the same contracts. The Exchange believes it is reasonable to continue to count such volume toward tier qualification under the sliding scale programs because it may prevent Floor Brokers from being disadvantaged under those programs as a result of executing orders against Market-Makers and is consistent with how such volume is counted today. The Exchange also believes it is reasonable to apply the same product exclusions that apply to the existing programs, so that the Floor Broker programs are administered consistently. The proposed rebate is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because it will be available equally to all Floor Brokers whose orders are executed against Market-Makers on the trading floor, and the treatment of such volume under the sliding scale programs will apply equally to all Floor Brokers. The Exchange believes it is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory to offer the rebate only to Floor Brokers, as Floor Brokers play an important role in bringing order flow to the trading floor, thereby enhancing liquidity and price discovery in open outcry.
The Exchange believes the proposed amendment to footnote 55 is reasonable because it applies the existing tier-based constant fee methodology, and the existing flat fees for Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM liquidity-adding and manual executions (as amended by this proposed rule change), additional binary index options. The Exchange believes it is reasonable to apply a single fee methodology to all Index Binaries because each shares the same binary payout structure, for which a fee that scales with the contract price is appropriate. The Exchange also believes it is reasonable to replace other references to XSP binary options in the Fees Schedule with references to Index Binaries because doing so treats all Index Binaries consistently, excluding them from the same incentive programs, volume calculations, caps, and surcharges from which XSP binary options are currently excluded, and avoids the need to enumerate each Index Binary in multiple provisions of the Fees Schedule. These changes are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the same formula, tier-based constants, and flat fees (as applicable) will apply uniformly to all market participants within each applicable capacity in all Index Binaries, and all market participants will be subject to the same program exclusions with respect to all Index Binaries.
The Exchange believes the proposed fee holiday for Cboe Options Market-Maker/DPM/LMM orders in Index Binaries executed electronically and adding liquidity is reasonable because it will reduce costs for Market-Makers and is designed to encourage Market-Makers to provide liquidity and quote competitively in Index Binaries, which benefits all market participants through tighter markets and increased trading opportunities. The Exchange believes it is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory to apply the fee holiday only to Market-Makers because Market-Makers, unlike other market participants, are subject to quoting obligations and add value through continuous liquidity provision, and the fee holiday will apply equally to all Market-Makers. The Exchange believes that assessing a flat fee of $0.01 per contract for Index Binaries where the premium is greater than or equal to $1.00 is reasonable because it simplifies and streamlines the fees applicable to such transactions and represents a modest decrease from the estimated current fees of $0.01184 (for Customers) and $0.01386 (for Non-Customers) per contract. The proposed change is equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the same $0.01 fee will apply to all capacities.
The Exchange believes the proposed Flex AIM Response Fee and FLEX break-up credit are reasonable because they are designed to protect the price discovery efforts of market participants that bring FLEX orders to the Exchange for execution in FLEX AIM and FLEX SAM auctions and to compensate Customer Agency orders whose volume is broken up by AIM Responses, which the Exchange believes will encourage market participants to continue to execute FLEX transactions on the Exchange rather than on other exchanges or in the over-the-counter market. The Exchange believes it is reasonable to assess the fee on AIM Responses, as responders benefit from the price discovery provided by the initiating party, and to pay a portion of that amount to Customer Agency orders as a credit. The Exchange believes it is reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory to limit the credit to Customer Agency orders because the existing Break-Up Credits are likewise directed to Customer Agency orders. The Exchange also believes it is reasonable to exclude FLEX Micros from the fee and credit, consistent with the exclusion of FLEX Micros from other incentive programs and surcharges under the Fees Schedule. The proposed fee and credit are equitable and not unfairly discriminatory because the fee will apply equally to all AIM Responses in FLEX AIM and FLEX SAM auctions regardless of capacity, and the credit will apply equally to all Customer Agency orders that are broken up by an AIM Response, in both Multiply Listed and proprietary products.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed changes will apply
(
printed page 74266)
uniformly to all similarly situated market participants. The proposed changes to QCC fees and credits will apply equally to all TPHs that execute QCC orders, the proposed Market-Maker manual transaction fees will apply equally to all Market-Makers, the proposed Floor Broker Program and related amendments to the Floor Broker sliding scale programs will apply equally to all Floor Brokers, the SPX/SPXW Electronic Execution Surcharge and other provisions that reference SPXW will apply to SPXO in the same manner as they apply to SPXW, the existing Index Binaries fee methodology, flat fees (as amended), and program exclusions will apply uniformly to all market participants in all Index Binaries, the Index Binaries fee holiday will apply equally to all Market-Makers, and the Flex AIM Response Fee and FLEX break-up credit will apply equally to all FLEX AIM and FLEX SAM Responses and all Customer Agency orders, respectively. As discussed above, the Exchange believes the proposed changes are designed to incentivize additional order flow to the Exchange, which benefits all market participants through increased liquidity and trading opportunities.
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. In particular, the proposed Market-Maker manual fees and Floor Broker Program are in line with fees and rebates recently adopted by NYSE Arca, NYSE American, Nasdaq PHLX, and MIAX Sapphire for comparable floor transactions, and therefore reflect, rather than burden, intermarket competition. With respect to the Exchange's other proposed fee changes, the Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which market participants can readily direct order flow to competing venues, including other options exchanges and off-exchange venues, if they deem fee levels at a particular venue to be excessive or incentives to be insufficient. The Exchange believes the proposed changes reflect this competitive environment and are designed to attract additional order flow to the Exchange.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106900; File No. SR-NYSE-2026-37]
November 13, 2026.
I. Introduction
On July 31, 2026, New York Stock Exchange LLC (“NYSE” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”), pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
a proposed rule change to amend Sections 303A.00 and 303A.07 of the NYSE Listed Company Manual (“Manual”) to extend the transition period in which a listed company must establish and internal audit function. The proposed rule change was published for comment in the
Federal Register
on August 18, 2026.
[
3
]
On September 25, 2026, pursuant to Section 19(b)(2) of the Act,
[
4
]
the Commission designated a longer period within which to take action on the proposed rule change.
[
5
]
The Commission is instituting proceedings pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act
[
6
]
to determine whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change.
II. Description of the Proposed Rule Change
Section 303A.07(c) of the Manual states that each company listed on the Exchange must have an internal audit function. The Exchange states that the purpose of the internal audit function is to provide an issuer's management and audit committee with ongoing assessments of the issuer's risk management processes and system of internal controls.
[
7
]
The function may be outsourced to a third-party service provider other than an issuer's independent auditor.
Sections 303A.00 and 303A.07 of the Manual provide a transition period for certain issuers to become compliant with the internal audit function.
[
8
]
Pursuant to Section 303A.07, issuers must have an internal audit function in place no later than the first anniversary of their listing date. The Exchange proposes to extend the transition period to implement an internal audit function from one year to five years.
According to the Exchange, issuers have expressed concern that developing a capable internal audit function within the first year of listing presents challenges as issuers adjust to life as a newly public company. In expressing concern over the current one-year compliance period, issuers often cite competing business and regulatory obligations requiring management's attention and the challenges of building an internal audit function to assess a company's internal control environment while a company is still in its early stages and continuing to grow. The Exchange states that it believes that having a robust internal audit function is a key component of sound corporate governance, but agrees that providing issuers with additional time to develop such function will result in a more effective function.
[
9
]
The Exchange further states that, during the proposed five-year transition period, other requirements will continue to provide sufficient assurance that issuers listed on the Exchange are appropriately managing risk. All issuers listed on the Exchange are required to have an Audit Committee comprised of at least three independent directors.
[
10
]
The Audit Committee of an issuer listed on the Exchange must have a written charter that requires it to “at least annually, obtain and review a report by the [company's] independent auditor describing: the firm's internal quality-control procedures; any material issues
(
printed page 74222)
raised by the most recent internal quality-control review.”
[
11
]
In addition, Section 404(a) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act
[
12
]
obligates management to maintain an adequate internal control structure for financial reporting and annually assess its effectiveness. Section 404(b) of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act
[
13
]
requires a company's independent auditor to provide an attestation on management's internal control assessment. In addition, the CEO and CFO certifications required by Sections 302 and 906 of the Sarbanes-Oxley Act
[
14
]
require an additional level of management responsibility for internal control oversight. The Exchange states that the Sarbanes-Oxley Act and its provisions discussed herein was enacted after the Exchange first adopted its internal audit requirement and that, in this regard, the internal audit function may be viewed as a supplement for the statutory protections embodied in the Sarbanes-Oxley Act.
[
15
]
The Exchange also states that Nasdaq Stock Market (“Nasdaq”) does not require companies listed on that exchange to maintain an internal audit function.
[
16
]
III. Proceedings To Determine Whether To Approve or Disapprove SR-NYSEAMER-2026-17 and Grounds for Disapproval Under Consideration
The Commission is instituting proceedings pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act
[
17
]
to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved. Institution of such proceedings is appropriate at this time in view of the legal and policy issues raised by the proposed rule change. Institution of proceedings does not indicate that the Commission has reached any conclusions with respect to any of the issues involved. Rather, as described below, the Commission seeks and encourages interested persons to provide additional comment on the proposed rule change to inform the Commission's analysis of whether to approve or disapprove the proposed rule change.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(2)(B) of the Act,
[
18
]
the Commission is providing notice of the grounds for disapproval under consideration. The Commission is instituting proceedings to allow for additional analysis of, and input from commenters with respect to, the proposed rule change's consistency with the Act, and in particular, Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
19
]
which requires, among other things, that the rules of a national securities exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest, and not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
As discussed above, the Exchange's proposal would extend the transition period in which a listed company must establish an internal audit function from one year to five years. The Commission has received a significant number of comment letters on the proposed rule change, most of which oppose the proposal.
[
20
]
Commenters state, among other things, that the period of time immediately following initial listing is precisely when independent oversight matters most and that the alternative safeguards mentioned in the proposal are not adequate substitutes for an internal audit function.
[
21
]
The Commission asks that commenters address the sufficiency of the Exchange's statements in support of the proposal, which are set forth in the Notice, in addition to any other comments they may wish to submit about the proposed rule change. In particular, the Commission seeks comment on whether the proposal to change the transition period for newly listed companies to establish an internal audit function from one year to five years includes sufficient analysis to support a conclusion that the proposal is consistent with the requirements of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act.
[
22
]
The Commission also seeks comment on the issues raised by commenters.
[
23
]
IV. Procedure: Request for Written Comments
The Commission requests that interested persons provide written submissions of their data, views, and arguments with respect to the issues identified above, including the issues raised by commenters, as well as any other concerns they may have with the proposal. In particular, the Commission invites the written views of interested persons concerning whether the proposed rule change is consistent with Sections 6(b)(5), or any other provision of the Act, or the rules and regulations thereunder. Although there do not appear to be any issues relevant to approval or disapproval that would be facilitated by an oral presentation of data, views, and arguments, the Commission will consider, pursuant to Rule 19b-4 under the Act,
[
24
]
any request for an opportunity to make an oral presentation.
[
25
]
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views, and arguments regarding whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved by December 9, 2026. Any person who wishes to file a rebuttal to any other person's submission must file that rebuttal by December 23, 2026. The Commission asks that commenters address the sufficiency of the Exchange's statements in support of the proposal, in addition to any other comments they may wish to submit about the proposed rule change.
Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSE-2026-37 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSE-2026-37. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​
(
printed page 74223)
rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSE-2026-37 and should be submitted by December 9, 2026. Rebuttal comments should be submitted by December 23, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
26
]
J. Matthew DeLesDernier,
Deputy Secretary.

November 13, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”),
[
1

[

notice is hereby given that on November 3, 2026, The Nasdaq Stock Market LLC (“Nasdaq” or “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“SEC” or “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II, below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to provide transparency to the process for selection of an initial trading date and time for new listings.
The text of the proposed rule change is set forth below; proposed new language is italic; deleted text is in brackets.
*

The NASDAQ Stock Market LLC Rules
*

5200. General Procedures and Prerequisites for Initial and Continued Listing on The Nasdaq Stock Market
5205. The Applications and Qualifications Process
(a)-(i) No change.
(j) Once Nasdaq approves a Company's application to list a security, the security will begin trading on Nasdaq on a date and, where applicable, at a quotation time, that is mutually agreed upon by Nasdaq and the Company.
*
*
*
*
*
(b) Not applicable.
(c) Not applicable.
*

The text of the proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
https://listingcenter.nasdaq.com/​rulebook/​nasdaq/​rulefilings
,
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
(
printed page 74224)
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
Nasdaq proposes to adopt new Listing Rule 5205(j), which will specify that, once a company's application to list a security is approved, the security will begin trading on Nasdaq on a date and at a time that is mutually agreed upon by Nasdaq and the company. Nasdaq believes that including this requirement in its rules will add transparency to Nasdaq's process of scheduling initial public offerings and other new listings.
After a security has been approved for listing, Nasdaq works with the issuing company and its advisors to schedule a preferred initial trading date, which may in unusual circumstances be moved by either Nasdaq or the company due to market conditions, company preference or other events where launch is not in the interests of investors or the market. In the case of an initial listing that uses the Nasdaq IPO Halt Cross
[
3
]
to initiate trading, Nasdaq will also establish, in conjunction with the company and its underwriter or financial advisor (as applicable), a time to commence the “Pre-Launch Period.” No date or time would ever be selected without the agreement of the company, and the Exchange expects that companies will coordinate with their underwriter or financial advisors, as applicable, when selecting the date and time.
While this has been Nasdaq's longstanding practice, and confusion has not previously occurred, Nasdaq believes it will aid transparency to modify its rules to explicitly state that trading will begin on a date, and at a time, that is mutually agreed upon by Nasdaq and the listing company.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that its proposal is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
4
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(5) of the Act,
[
5
]
in particular, in that it is designed to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general to protect investors and the public interest, by adding transparency to how the date and time for the initiation of trading is selected. Further, requiring the mutual agreement of Nasdaq and the company will enhance investor protection in rare instances where market conditions, company preference or other events make the selection of a certain day or time suboptimal.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The proposed rule change merely reflects how Nasdaq, together with the listing company, determines the trading date for new securities and will not have any burden on competition.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were either solicited or received.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
6
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
7
]
thereunder. Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
8
]
and subparagraph (f)(6) of Rule 19b-4
[
9
]
thereunder.
A proposed rule change filed under Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
10
]
normally does not become operative prior to 30 days after the date of the filing. However, pursuant to Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii),
[
11
]
the Commission may designate a shorter time if such action is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. The Exchange has asked the Commission to waive the 30-day operative delay so that the proposed rule change may become operative immediately upon filing. The Exchange states that the proposed change provides transparency to Nasdaq's current practice of establishing the day and time for a security to initially trade and would codify this practice, making no change to how listings are scheduled. The Exchange further states that waiving the operative delay will eliminate any potential confusion as to the mechanism for selecting a date and time during that delayed period. For these reasons, and because the proposed rule change raises no new or novel legal or regulatory issues, the Commission finds that waiver of the 30-day operative delay is consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest. Therefore, the Commission waives the 30-day operative delay and designates the proposed rule change operative upon filing.
[
12
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
(

https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml

Paper Comments

All submissions should refer to file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-097. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NASDAQ-2026-097 and should be submitted on or before December 9, 2026.

The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the NYSE American Options Fee Schedule (“Fee Schedule”) to lower certain initiating participant rebates related to Customer Best Execution (“CUBE”) Auctions. The Exchange proposes to implement the fee change effective November 2, 2026. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The purpose of this filing is to lower certain initiating participant rebates related to CUBE Auctions.
[
4
]
The Exchange proposes to implement the fee change effective November 2, 2026.
[
5
]
Background
The Exchange has established various pricing incentives designed to encourage increased electronic volume executed on the Exchange, including, but not limited to, the American Customer Engagement (“ACE”) Program.
[
6
]
To encourage participation in the ACE Program and CUBE Auctions, the Exchange offers an ACE Initiating Participant Rebate to ACE Program participants that initiate Single-Leg CUBE Auctions,
[
7
]
Complex CUBE Auctions,
[
8
]
and AON Single-Leg or AON Complex CUBE Auctions.
[
9
]
Currently, the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate for each of these auctions $0.115 per contact for all issues (
i.e.,
penny and non-penny).
In addition, the Exchange offers the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate that enables non-ACE Program participants to qualify for this Rebate on certain initiating Complex CUBE Auctions provided they meet certain
(
printed page 74242)
monthly volume qualification levels and increase their initiating CUBE volume.
[
10
]
Currently, the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate is $0.115 per contract for all issues.
The Exchange proposes to reduce the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate for all three auctions and the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate, for Complex CUBE Auctions, from $0.115 per contract to $0.105 per contract across all issues. The proposed change is the result of the Exchange's ongoing reassessment and rebalancing of its fee structure overall and, in this instance, its CUBE rebate structure.
[
11
]
The proposal only slightly reduces the amount of the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Participant Rebate where applicable. As such, the Exchange believes that the Rebates will continue to encourage ATP Holders to initiate CUBE Auctions, whether single-leg, complex, or AON.
The change will apply equally to all similarly situated market participants. Moreover, the Exchange believes all market participants stand to benefit from the continuing increased order flow, which promotes market depth, facilitates tighter spreads and enhances price discovery. Increased order flow promotes market depth, facilitates tighter spreads and enhances price discovery, which enhances market quality for all participants.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Act,
[
12
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Sections 6(b)(4) and (5) of the Act,
[
13
]
in particular, because it provides for the equitable allocation of reasonable dues, fees, and other charges among its members, issuers and other persons using its facilities and does not unfairly discriminate between customers, issuers, brokers or dealers.
As a threshold matter, the Exchange is subject to significant competitive forces in the market for options securities transaction services that constrain its pricing determinations in that market. The Commission has repeatedly expressed its preference for competition over regulatory intervention in determining prices, products, and services in the securities markets. In Regulation NMS, the Commission highlighted the importance of market forces in determining prices and SRO revenues and, also, recognized that current regulation of the market system “has been remarkably successful in promoting market competition in its broader forms that are most important to investors and listed companies.”
[
14
]
There are currently 20 registered options exchanges competing for order flow. Based on publicly available information and, excluding index-based options, no single exchange has more than 16% of the market share of executed volume of multiply-listed equity and ETF options trades.
[
15
]
Therefore, currently no exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of multiply-listed equity and ETF options order flow. More specifically, in September 2026, the Exchange had 12.39% market share of executed volume of multiply-listed equity and ETF options order flow. In such a low concentrated and highly competitive market, no single options exchange possesses significant pricing power in the execution of option order flow.
In response to these competitive forces and as discussed herein, the Exchange has established various pricing incentives regarding its CUBE Auctions, including, but not limited to, the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate, the Alternative Initiating Rebate and Professional Volume Incentive Initiating Participant Rebate, which are designed to encourage ATP Holders to utilize the CUBE Auction and to direct (increased) volume to the Exchange.
The Exchange believes that the proposed changes in the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Rebate are reasonable, equitable, and not unfairly discriminatory and will continue to provide the intended incentive for ATP Holders to utilize the CUBE Auctions on the Exchange. To the extent this purpose is achieved, the Exchange believes that the proposed CUBE rebate would not discourage ATP Holders from directing activity to the Exchange. The Exchange also believes that the proposal represents an equitable allocation of credits and is not unfairly discriminatory because the proposal will apply equally to all similarly situated ATP Holders.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
In accordance with Section 6(b)(8) of the Act, the Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change would impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act.
Intramarket Competition.
The Exchange believes that the proposed changes to the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Rebate would not affect intramarket competition because, as noted above, it would impact all market participants equally and, therefore, would not impose a disparate burden on competition among market participants on the Exchange. Similarly, the proposed changes are designed to continue to attract order flow to the Exchange by offering ATP Holders competitive incentives to continue to direct their order flow to the Exchange, thereby increasing liquidity to the benefit of all market participants.
Intermarket Competition.
The Exchange believes that the proposed changes to the ACE Initiating Participant Rebate and the Alternative Initiating Rebate would not affect intermarket competition. As noted above, the Exchange operates in a highly competitive market in which the Exchange must continually adjust its fees and rebates to remain competitive with other exchanges and to attract order flow to the Exchange. The proposed change reflects this competitive reality.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The foregoing rule change is effective upon filing pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)
[
16
]
of the Act and subparagraph (f)(2) of Rule 19b-4
[
17
]
thereunder, because it establishes a due, fee, or other charge imposed by the Exchange.
At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may
(
printed page 74243)
temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
18
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-101 on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-101. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEAMER-2026-101 and should be submitted on or before December 9, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
19
]
J. Matthew DeLesDernier,
Deputy Secretary.
